title: Marella Payments — pilot outreach brain dump
content:
Context:
- Target: Marella Payments — mid-market payments processor (EU-first), ~120 engineers, serves ~2,000 merchants (ecommerce + POS).
- Why we care: clear use-case for hosted embeddings/reranking for fraud signals and conversational merchant support. Potential Dedicated or Private sale due to PCI/data residency.
- Outreach goal: get a technical pilot with Product/Platform team (CTO + Head of Payments Ops). Pilot scope: inference for merchant support triage + a small reranking experiment for fraud alert prioritization.

High-level executive thesis (for quick email intros):
- Safe, high-throughput LLM inference without building and operating GPU infra.
- Options: Hosted API (fast), Dedicated pools (predictable SLOs), Private (VPC, customer KMS) — matches Marella compliance needs.

Key stakeholders (hypothesis) — confirm on intro call:
- CTO: Tomas Weber — cares about uptime, control plane access, SLA, KMS integration.
- Head of Product (merchant UX): Emilia Kors — cares about latency, accuracy of reranks, UX flow.
- Head of Ops / Security: Marco Ibarra — PCI, audit logs, data retention, on-prem contract.
- Platform Eng lead: likely to own integration (k8s, queues).

Notes from public signals & quick scrape:
- Marella blog (June): expanding into DACH, note on stricter data-residency asks from larger merchants.
- Tech hiring: multiple infra+security roles -> signal readiness for integrations.
- Compliance: advertises PCI DSS Level 1.

Technical fit and pilot design (draft):
1) Pilot 1 — Support triage assistant (NLP classification + contextual generation):
   - Ingest: anonymized support transcripts (first 90 days) + merchant metadata
   - Output: predicted intent, severity, suggested reply snippets (tokens limited, deterministic prompts)
   - SLO: p50 latency < 300ms for short support messages (hosted path) or <150ms (dedicated)
   - Privacy: redact PAN and any PCI-sensitive fields before sending to Redwood-hosted environment; offer Private with customer KMS if they insist.
   - Eval: human-in-the-loop review on 500 sampled replies, target accuracy uplift + reduced TTR for agents.

2) Pilot 2 — Fraud alert reranker (batch):
   - Inputs: existing fraud model scores + merchant metadata + candidate alerts -> rank top alerts for manual review
   - Throughput: batch job ~10k alerts/day initially; scaling plan to 100k/day
   - Metric: reviewer precision@10, reduction in false positives, time saved per reviewer

Pricing posture (for pilot discussion):
- Default: usage-based (tokens) for Hosted.
- Pilot discount: flat monthly pilot fee + capped token allowance (covers experimentation).
- Dedicated/Private: commit-based pricing; show 3-tier options (small: 1-2 GPUs, med: 4-8, large: 12+) with clear throughput/latency numbers.
- Key ask: understand Marella's expected qps, avg tokens/request to produce an accurate pilot quote.

Objections & scripts (quick):
- "We have to keep everything on-prem for PCI":
  - Acknowledge ("totally reasonable"). Offer Private with VPC/on-prem install + KMS/HSM integration; propose security workshop and reference SOC2 + customer audit reports.
- "Latency will be too high":
  - Ask for 3 sample request patterns (tokens, concurrency). Offer Dedicated pool and local region routing; show real numbers from similar merchants (p50 120–180ms on dedicated).
- "Cost concerns / building ourselves":
  - Frame as total cost of ownership vs dev+infra+ops. Provide modeled runbook: 3 FTE ops + infra vs Redwood managed + lower per-token cost due to batching/kv cache. Offer a 6-week pilot to generate real metrics.

Outbound sequence (concise drafts) — pick channel: email then LinkedIn then two follow-ups:
- Subject: Quick pilot idea: reduce Marella support toil by ~30%
- Email 1 (short):
  Hi Emilía/Tomas —
  Quick note: we’ve been helping payments platforms reduce support time and false-positive fraud alerts with a small, measurable pilot (Redwood Inference). We can run a 6-week experiment using anonymized transcripts and fraud logs — no infra changes required, and we support Private deployment if you need PCI isolation.
  Want 20–30 mins next week to sketch scope and success metrics?
  — Sana

- Follow-up #1 (if no reply after 4 days): short ping + 1-sentence case study + Calendly link.
- LinkedIn touch: mention shared connection and point to pilot one-pager.

Success metrics to propose on discovery call:
- Agent-reported helpfulness (Likert) and TTR reduction target: 20–30%
- Precision@10 for fraud reranker > baseline by X (quantify after data sample)
- Production SLOs: uptime 99.9% and p95 latency targets for API calls under stated concurrency.

Info we need from Marella before we can quote: (these are critical — add to call checklist)
- Typical RPS and peak concurrency (per tenant/overall)
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + response) for support messages and rerank candidates
- Data retention / redaction rules and whether they can provide anonymized sample data
- Regulatory constraints: particular EU region(s) required for data residency
- Monster cases: 95th percentile prompt length, and batch sizes for rerank jobs
- Who will own integration on their side? Slack/webhook/kafka details?

Risk map / gating items:
- Legal: Review Data Processing Agreement + encryption in transit & at rest — must get Legal looped early.
- Security: They might require penetration test reports + code review for Private. Prep a template security checklist.
- Compliance: If they require on-prem only, timeline jumps to months (coord with Eng/Private team).

Competition & positioning notes (what to play up):
- AWS Bedrock / Anthropic: position Redwood as production-ops focused + predictable economics (dedicated pools, rollout & fallback policies).
- In-house infra: emphasize we handle batching, KV caching, and SLOs out of box (avoid the 3 FTE ops trap).

Materials to prepare before call (owner initials):
- Pilot one-pager (Sana) — short 1-pager w/ scope, timeline, SLAs, pricing
- Security checklist + SOC2 summary (Liam)
next_steps:
1) Send intro email draft to Tomas/Emilia (Sana) — today. 2) Create pilot one-pager and attach to follow-up (Sana, due 11/10). 3) Slack intro to account exec (Ava) and ask for recent Marella contact list. 4) Engage Solutions Eng (ticket INFR-342) to evaluate Dedicated/Private feasibility for their qps. 5) Prep security artifacts (Liam)

Open questions:
- Can Marella provide a 1-week sample of anonymized transcripts? If no, how will we validate accuracy?
- Are there internal vetoes for using any external LLM provider? Who signs off?

Random scribbles / possible lines to test in outreach:
- "We can run the pilot in your VPC with your KMS in 2–3 weeks"
- "Pilot commitment: 6 weeks, two milestones (prototype -> live A/B test)"
- "We limit token retention to X days for pilot and can purge logs on demand"
